remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive. Original in clay; completed in New York, shortly after the death of O'Keeffe's mother on 1 May 1916. Most probably intended as a memento mori. Pictured in 1917 New York (291) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 7. "Did you treat your Clay friend [clay sculpture] to a bus ride –– Did she visit 291 –– Was the Man out [Stieglitz] –– was the lady cast –– did she smash" (Anita Pollitzer to O'Keeffe, 18 June 1916, *Lovingly Georgia* [1990], p. 158). "I did not take the thing to 291 but had it cast –– the man sent me one but he has another –– the way he fixed the pedestal is awful –– I don't know about the rest of it –– I have hardly looked at it" (O'Keeffe to Anita Pollitzer, June 1916, *Lovingly Georgia* [1990], p. 159). (Source: Lynes, 1999)
